collection.label: Edicts of Ashoka
collection.author_name: Ashoka (Devanampriya Priyadarsin), Maurya king (r. c. 268-232 BCE)
collection.critical_edition: E. Hultzsch, Inscriptions of Asoka (CII I, 1925), transliteration read from the scan
collection.search_terms: ashoka asoka edicts rock edicts pillar edicts maurya brahmi prakrit dhamma dharma kalinga girnar kalsi devanampiya piyadasi buddhist inscriptions
collection.description: The edicts of the Maurya king Ashoka (c. 260-232 BCE), the earliest datable writing in India, rock by rock: E. Hultzsch's 1925 transliteration and English, each edict shown on the inked impression of the stone that carries it.

texts.title: Edicts of Ashoka at Girnar: the fourteen Major Rock Edicts
texts.date_approx: c. 256 BCE (edicts dated 12 and 13 years after Ashoka's consecration)
texts.source: Girnar, near Junagadh (Gujarat), rock inscription of Ashoka; Hultzsch's collotype plates of inked impressions (1925); Hultzsch's transliteration and English (CII I, 1925), read from the archive.org scan
texts.description: Ashoka's fourteen Major Rock Edicts on the Girnar rock in Gujarat (c. 256 BCE): Hultzsch's transliteration of the Prakrit text and his 1925 English, edict by edict, each with the impression of the lines that carry it.

texts.title: Edicts of Ashoka at Kalsi: the fourteen Major Rock Edicts
texts.date_approx: c. 256 BCE (edicts dated 12 and 13 years after Ashoka's consecration)
texts.source: Kalsi, near Dehradun (Uttarakhand), rock inscription of Ashoka; Hultzsch's collotype plates of inked impressions (1925); Hultzsch's transliteration and English (CII I, 1925), read from the archive.org scan
texts.description: Ashoka's fourteen Major Rock Edicts on the Kalsi rock (c. 256 BCE), with the fullest Brahmi text of Edict XIII on the conquest of Kalinga and the Greek kings: Hultzsch's transliteration and 1925 English, each edict with the impression of the lines that carry it.

texts.title: Edicts of Ashoka at Dhauli: the two Separate Edicts to the officers of Tosali
texts.date_approx: c. 256 BCE (undated; issued with the Major Rock Edicts in conquered Kalinga)
texts.source: Dhauli, near Bhubaneswar (Odisha), rock inscription of Ashoka; Hultzsch's collotype plates of inked impressions (1925); Hultzsch's transliteration and English (CII I, 1925), read from the archive.org scan
texts.description: The two Separate Edicts at Dhauli in Kalinga, in which Ashoka tells the officers of Tosali that all men are his children and how to treat prisoners and the unconquered border peoples: Hultzsch's transliteration and 1925 English, each with the inked impression of the rock.

pages.caption: Dhauli, First Separate Rock Edict (inked impression, Hultzsch 1925)
Dhauli, Second Separate Rock Edict (inked impression, Hultzsch 1925)

texts.title: Edicts of Ashoka on the Delhi-Topra pillar: the seven Pillar Edicts
texts.date_approx: c. 243-242 BCE (edicts dated 26 and 27 years after Ashoka's consecration)
texts.source: Delhi-Topra pillar, Firoz Shah Kotla, Delhi (originally at Topra, Haryana), pillar inscription of Ashoka; Hultzsch's collotype plates of inked impressions (1925); Hultzsch's transliteration and English (CII I, 1925), read from the archive.org scan
texts.description: The seven Pillar Edicts of Ashoka on the Delhi-Topra pillar (c. 243-242 BCE), the only pillar with all seven, including the long seventh edict on the Dharma-mahamatras and the religious communities: Hultzsch's transliteration and 1925 English, each edict with the impression of the face that carries it.

texts.title: Ashoka's Rummindei (Lumbini) pillar inscription: the birthplace of the Buddha
texts.date_approx: c. 249 BCE (20 years after Ashoka's consecration)
texts.source: Rummindei (Lumbini), Nepal, pillar inscription of Ashoka; Hultzsch's collotype plates of inked impressions (1925); photograph of the stone (Wikimedia Commons); Hultzsch's transliteration and English (CII I, 1925), read from the archive.org scan
texts.description: Ashoka's five-line inscription on the pillar at Lumbini (c. 249 BCE), recording his visit to the birthplace of the Buddha Sakyamuni: Hultzsch's transliteration and 1925 English, with a photograph of the inscription on the pillar and an inked impression.

pages.caption: Rummindei (Lumbini), Rummindei pillar inscription (photograph)
Rummindei (Lumbini), Rummindei pillar inscription (inked impression, Hultzsch 1925)

texts.title: Ashoka's Nigali Sagar pillar inscription: the stupa of the Buddha Konakamana
texts.date_approx: c. 254 BCE and c. 249 BCE (14 and [20] years after Ashoka's consecration)
texts.source: Nigali Sagar (Nigliva), Nepal, pillar inscription of Ashoka; Hultzsch's collotype plates of inked impressions (1925); Hultzsch's transliteration and English (CII I, 1925), read from the archive.org scan
texts.description: Ashoka's four-line inscription on the Nigali Sagar pillar in Nepal, recording that he enlarged the stupa of the Buddha Konakamana: Hultzsch's transliteration and 1925 English, with the inked impression of the stone.

pages.caption: Nigali Sagar (Nigliva), Nigali Sagar pillar inscription (inked impression, Hultzsch 1925)

texts.title: Ashoka's Calcutta-Bairat (Bhabru) inscription: the edict that names Buddhist texts
texts.source: Calcutta-Bairat boulder, Asiatic Society, Kolkata (found near Bairat, Rajasthan), boulder inscription of Ashoka; Hultzsch's collotype plates of inked impressions (1925); Hultzsch's transliteration and English (CII I, 1925), read from the archive.org scan
texts.description: Ashoka's letter to the Buddhist Sangha on the Calcutta-Bairat stone, the only edict that names Buddhist scriptures: Hultzsch's transliteration and 1925 English, with the inked impression of the stone.

pages.caption: Calcutta-Bairat boulder, Calcutta-Bairat rock inscription (inked impression, Hultzsch 1925)
